acme_ops: Hi support — started getting a bunch of 429s and some 401/402s this morning after a maintenance window. It looks like generation calls fail intermittently. Example error: `{\n  \"error\": \"rate_limit_exceeded\",\n  \"message\": \"Request quota exceeded for model rwd-3-32k\"\n}`. Happening across multiple endpoints (generate + streaming). Not sure if auth or billing. Anyone seen this?

alex_support: Thanks — can you paste the full error response (headers + body) and the model + approximate concurrency? Also any X-Request-ID you see. We’ll check quotas and billing.

acme_ops: Request id: `req_01HxyzA7Q2B8C9`. Using model `rwd-3-32k`, context ~18k tokens per request, concurrent clients ~30 (we ramped up today). Quick repro loop below — runs ~60 requests/min and then 429s start.

```bash
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-3-32k\",\"input\":\"'"$(head -c 18000 /dev/urandom | base64)"'\"}' 
  | jq .
  sleep 0.8
done
```

alex_support: That repro helps. Two quick things: (1) long contexts are very expensive and count heavily against TPM/RPM, (2) per-model concurrency caps can cause 429s if you exceed them even if overall account tokens look ok.

maria_eng: FYI the hosted default soft-limits for `rwd-3-32k` are usually in the ballpark of RPM=300, TPM=3000 (these are soft and vary by account), and max concurrency ~16 for standard accounts. If you run 30 concurrent streams with ~18k tokens each you can exhaust the token budget very fast and trigger 429s or backend throttling.

jordan_sre: Can you run `curl -I` or print response headers from one of the failing responses? We often send headers like `x-ratelimit-limit-rpm`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, and `x-model-max-concurrency` that are helpful. Also look for `x-account-status` / `x-billing-hold`.

acme_ops: Pasting headers from one failure:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:22:11 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: req_01HxyzA7Q2B8C9
x-ratelimit-limit-rpm: 300
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 60
x-ratelimit-limit-tpm: 3000
x-model-max-concurrency: 16
Content-Length: 123

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Model concurrency exceeded or per-model TPM exhausted"}
```

alex_support: That header set is super useful — it shows you hit the RPM/TMP budget and the model-level concurrency cap (16). Two separate issues are visible: the token/quota exhaustion and the concurrency cap.

maria_eng: Quick mitigation: reduce parallelism to <=12 to avoid hitting the model concurrency ceiling, and backoff on 429s with exponential jitter. If you need sustained throughput at these token sizes, we recommend a Dedicated pool or raising soft limits via support so we can provision more capacity.

jordan_sre: Also note billing insight — if billing fails we sometimes serve mixed 402/429/401 responses depending on which control plane check fails first. Can you confirm billing status? @billing_bot can you paste the account hold state for `acme-corp`?

billing_bot: :warning: Billing hold detected for account `acme-corp`. Last invoice unpaid: invoice_2026_05_11. Payment method failed on 2026-05-11. Follow https://billing.redwood.inference/account/acme-corp/invoices to resolve.

acme_ops: Oh snap — we rotated cards earlier and one of them failed. Just updated card in the dashboard. Is there a way to force quota re-eval or clear the soft throttle?

alex_support: Thanks for updating the card. I’ve opened a billing ticket to clear the hold and requested a temporary soft-limit lift for 48–72h while you validate. In the meantime, please reduce concurrency and add backoff. I’ll paste a suggested backoff snippet.

```js
// simple exponential backoff for client retries
async function retry(fn, retries=5) {
  for (let i=0;i<retries;i++){
    try { return await fn(); }
    catch (e) {
      if (e.status !== 429) throw e;
      const wait = Math.min(1000 * 2**i, 10000) + Math.floor(Math.random()*200);
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, wait));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('retries exhausted');
}
```

maria_eng: Additional technical notes: long single-request contexts are charged token-by-token, so one 18k-token request is the same bucket hit as many smaller requests summing to 18k. Consider sliding-window retrieval (retrieve top-k + shorter prompt), or embeddings-based retrieval to keep prompt size < 4–8k for production workloads if possible. Quantized or distilled model variants might also reduce token cost per second (lower compute), but TPM billing remains token-based.

acme_ops: Ran a test at 12 concurrent workers with jitter and switched to 8k token context — the 429s stopped, and headers now show `x-ratelimit-remaining: 89`. Thanks.

billing_bot: Payment processed for invoice_2026_05_11 :white_check_mark:. Billing hold cleared.

alex_support: Great, I’ve asked account ops to keep the temporary limit raise for 48h to let you finish testing. If you plan to keep this sustained throughput (18k contexts at high concurrency) we should discuss Dedicated/reserved capacity — ping @maria_eng to start an evaluation.

maria_eng: Happy to review. For predictable throughput at that token size we usually recommend Dedicated with autoscaling and custom concurrency/throughput profiles. I’ll DM next steps.

acme_ops: Appreciated — solution worked and billing fixed. We’ll start a Dedicated conversation. Thanks all. :pray:

alex_support: Closing here but leaving notes: root cause = combo of billing hold + hitting per-model concurrency / TPM limits. Action items: (1) account billed and hold cleared, (2) customer lowered concurrency + implemented backoff, (3) support requested temporary soft-limit increase, (4) Eng follow-up on Dedicated evaluation. Docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/limits#model-rpm-tpm-concurrency
